results.tides: TIDES. Ocean tides happen because the Moon's (and to a lesser extent the Sun's) gravity pulls more strongly on the side of Earth closer to it, stretching the ocean into a bulge on that side and, due to inertia, a corresponding bulge on the opposite side, while Earth's rotation carries coastlines through those bulges roughly twice a day.
results.autumn_leaves: LEAVES. Chlorophyll, the green pigment that dominates leaves in summer, breaks down as days shorten and temperatures cool, revealing yellow and orange pigments (carotenoids) that were there all along; reds and purples often form separately from sugars trapped in the leaf as it shuts down.
